paper.title: Efficient Contextual Bandits with Uninformed Feedback Graphs

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with uninformed feedback graphs, partially revealed graph setting
unmapped: Feedback graphs are stochastic, with mean adjacency realizable by a known graph class G (E[1{(i,j) in E_t}|x_t] = g*(x_t,i,j))
Only the out-neighbourhood A_t of the chosen action is revealed; the graph is never fully revealed
Learner has online square-loss regression oracle for F and online log-loss regression oracle for G with regret bounds Reg_Sq and Reg_Log
Learner knows alpha(G) (worst-case expected independence number over the graph class) and the oracle regret bounds to tune gamma
settings.definition_quote: In the \emph{partially revealed graph} setting, the learner does not observe anything else about the graph (other than $A_t$)... we assume that $G_t$ is always strongly observable

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with uninformed feedback graphs, fully revealed graph setting
unmapped: Feedback graphs are stochastic, with mean adjacency realizable by a known graph class G
Learner has online square-loss regression oracle for F and online log-loss regression oracle for G with regret bounds Reg_Sq and Reg_Log
Learner knows sum_t alpha_t and the oracle regret bounds to tune gamma
settings.definition_quote: while in the \emph{fully revealed graph} setting, the learner additionally observes the entire graph (that is, $E_t$).

symbols.alpha_calG: worst-case expected independence number over graph class G and contexts
symbols.Reg_Sq: regret bound of the online square-loss regression oracle for F
symbols.Reg_Log: regret bound of the online log-loss regression oracle for G

conditions: realizability of mean loss in F (Assumption 2.1)
realizability of mean graph in G (Assumption 2.3)
square-loss oracle regret bounded by Reg_Sq (Assumption 2.2)
log-loss oracle regret bounded by Reg_Log (Assumption 2.4)
tuning: gamma = max{4, sqrt(alpha(G) T log(KT) / max{Reg_Sq, Reg_Log})}

source.label: thm:partial
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{assum:loss}-\ref{asm:regression_oracle_graph} and partially revealed feedback graphs, \graphCBp with $\gamma=\max\left\{4,\sqrt{\frac{\alpha(\calG)T\log(KT)}{\max\{\RegSq,\RegLogG\}}}\right\}$ guarantees: \RegCB=\otil\left(\sqrt{\alpha(\calG) T\max\{\RegSq,\RegLogG\}}\right).

results.notes: Regret is defined via f* (mean losses), hence pseudo-regret against the best action per context. Õ hides log K, log T. The appendix shows a doubling-trick variant that reaches the same bound without knowing alpha(G).

symbols.sum_alpha_t: sum over rounds of alpha_t = alpha(g*, x_t), expected independence number of the true stochastic graph at round t
symbols.Reg_Sq: regret bound of the online square-loss regression oracle for F
symbols.Reg_Log: regret bound of the online log-loss regression oracle for G

conditions: realizability of mean loss in F (Assumption 2.1)
realizability of mean graph in G (Assumption 2.3)
square-loss oracle regret bounded by Reg_Sq (Assumption 2.2)
log-loss oracle regret bounded by Reg_Log (Assumption 2.4)
tuning: gamma = max{12, sqrt(sum_t alpha_t / max{Reg_Sq, Reg_Log})}

source.label: thm:fully
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{assum:loss}-\ref{asm:regression_oracle_graph} and fully revealed feedback graphs, \graphCBp with $\gamma=\max\left\{12,\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t}{\max\{\RegSq,\RegLogGF\}}}\right\}$ guarantees: \RegCB=\otil\left(\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t\max\{\RegSq,\RegLogGF\}}\right).

results.notes: The tuning needs sum_t alpha_t to be known. The paper says this matches the optimal rate in the informed setting.
